subject: Re: PLG credit issuance - suspected duplicate domains and bot signups
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Flagged PLG credit issuances - similar domains / disposable patterns

Jonas — quick heads up from the fraud experiments job. We observed a cluster of ~18 accounts created in the last 36 hours that received the self-serve PLG free credits. The accounts share the following signals:
- Same IP / proxied ASNs (high churn)
- Email domains with minor permutations of hollowai.io (eg hollowai-login.io, hollowai-svc.io)
- No active profile usage for first 12 hours, then burst token calls using embeddings endpoint

I pulled the signup export and a basic similarity score (attached). Please advise if we should pause further automatic credit issuance while we triage.

Actions I propose:
- Pause auto-credits for new signups from those domains
- Revoke credits for accounts with token consumption > 5k in first hour
- Notify sales to review HubSpot contacts for likely legit trials

Attachments: suspicious_signups_20260218.csv (CSV export, 18 rows)

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Platform Engineer — Abuse Detection
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Flagged PLG credit issuances - similar domains / disposable patterns

Thanks Dev — this looks actionable. Please:
1) Pause issuance of promotional free credits for signups from those domains immediately.
2) Revoke credits for any account in the CSV that exceeded 5k tokens in the first hour.
3) Keep a short audit of actions taken (who/when) and add to the ticket.

I'll loop in trust/abuse at HollowAI to see if these are known benign sandbox/test accounts or if they're synthetic. Neha / Lauren — please confirm if there are any open outbound sales threads for these domains (HubSpot links above) before we notify customers.

Subject: Fwd: PLG signups - possible disposable domains / bot activity

Hi HollowAI Trust team — forwarding a list of signups that look like permutations of your org's domain and a set of disposable variants. We want to confirm whether these are test/sandbox accounts you own or if they are externally created and potentially abusive.

Short context: our PLG flow grants a small free credit package on signup. Our system flagged a cluster of accounts that share IP patterns and identical profile metadata and then consumed tokens in a burst. We paused auto-issuance pending your confirmation.

Attached: suspicious_signups_20260218.csv (same file)

If these are benign test accounts, please reply with a short confirmation and we will reinstate credits for the whitelisted addresses. If not, we will proceed with revocation and a follow-up to sales/prospects.

Thanks for the quick look — appreciate a note back today if possible.

— Jonas

Update: executed actions per Jonas — summary below and log attached.

Summary of actions (18 accounts):
- Auto-issuance paused for matching domain patterns at 10:08 AM EST
- Credits revoked for 7 accounts that exceeded 5k tokens in the first hour
- Marked 3 accounts as "pending manual review" for Sales follow-up (HubSpot deals attached)

Audit log: revocation-log-20260218.txt (plain text) — includes account IDs, revocation timestamps, and operator id (dev_patel).

Recommendation: Sales (Jonas / Neha) to review HubSpot deals for the 3 pending accounts before we send a notification template. I pasted the HubSpot links in the ticket. If Sales confirms legit, we'll restore credits for those account IDs only.
